title: Bethell's Unbeaten 76 Sinks India at Old Trafford. Bishnoi's 29-Run Over Hands England a 1-0 Series Lead.
excerpt: Arshdeep took two wickets in the first over. Bethell took the match in the 17th. India trail in the five-match T20I series after a four-wicket loss in Manchester.
body:
Jacob Bethell walked to the crease with England reeling at 0 for 2 in the first over. He walked off, 46 balls later, having smashed an unbeaten 76 that dismantled India and handed the hosts a four-wicket win in the second T20 International at Old Trafford. England lead the five-match series 1-0 after the opener was washed out.

The defeat will sting. India had batted first and posted a competitive 190 for seven in their 20 overs, only to watch one man take it apart.

## Sooryavanshi Opens, Arshdeep Opens — Then the Middle Muddles

The drama started before the first delivery. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, India's 15-year-old debutant who broke Sachin Tendulkar's record as the youngest player to represent the country, was handed the opening slot in place of Sanju Samson.

He justified the selection immediately — a six over fine leg off Jofra Archer, another hoisted over the leg side off Josh Tongue — before Will Jacks' off-spin drew him down the track and Jos Buttler completed a sharp stumping. Sooryavanshi departed for 14 off 10, but his partnership of 50 with Abhishek Sharma (43 off 24) had set the tone.

Ishan Kishan (49 off 40) and captain Shreyas Iyer (37) added 65 for the third wicket, steadying the innings through the middle overs. But India could not push beyond 200. Three wickets fell for just 22 runs across overs 13-16 as Sam Curran (3/33) varied his pace beautifully. Tilak Varma's unbeaten 24 off 11 at the death rescued the total to a defensible 190.

Or so India thought.

## Arshdeep's Dream Over. Then Bethell's Nightmare One.

Arshdeep Singh produced the perfect start to the chase. Phil Salt edged the first ball of the innings behind. Jos Buttler, the England captain, clipped the fifth to mid-wicket where Varun Chakaravarthy clung on to a sharp catch. England: 0 for 2. Old Trafford fell silent.

Harry Brook counter-attacked with 39 off 15 — three sixes off Arshdeep in a single over — before Axar Patel had him caught behind off his glove while sweeping. Axar's four overs cost just 20 runs, his 100th T20 wicket for India, and for a while the spinners tightened the screws.

Bethell, though, never panicked. He and Tom Banton (39) rebuilt with a 67-run stand that kept England in touch. When Arshdeep returned to remove Banton, and Chakaravarthy trapped Will Jacks lbw, India needed 49 from the last five overs with only five wickets in hand.

What happened next will haunt Ravi Bishnoi.

**The 17th over went for 29 runs.** Bishnoi overstepped twice, gifting Bethell free hits on both occasions. The leg-spinner's no-ball habit — he had already overstepped earlier in the innings — handed England the momentum they barely deserved. Bethell smashed three towering sixes and a boundary in that single over, reaching his half-century amid a crescendo of noise from the Manchester crowd.

From there, the equation was a formality. Bishnoi finished with figures of 0/60 in four overs — the most expensive spell by an Indian spinner in a T20I this year. Although Harshit Rana removed Sam Curran, and Sooryavanshi celebrated a maiden international catch on the boundary, England needed only manageable runs from the last two overs.

Archer sealed it with two runs off the final ball of the 19th over.

## The Diaspora Scorecard

For the tens of thousands of Indian fans who packed Old Trafford — and millions more watching from living rooms across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom — the result was a gut-punch. India came into the tour as T20 World Cup champions, with a stacked squad featuring Kohli, Rohit, and Bumrah named in the subsequent ODI group. A bilateral T20 series loss in England was not part of the script.

**The series moves to Trent Bridge, Nottingham, on Tuesday, July 7** for the third T20I. India need to win three of the remaining four matches to take the series. Iyer's captaincy, Bishnoi's selection, and Samson's continued omission will all face scrutiny.

For NRIs in the UK, the next three matches are the best live-cricket viewing opportunity of the summer. Tickets for Trent Bridge (July 7), Edgbaston (July 10), and The Oval (July 12) are still available — and after this result, the atmosphere will be electric.

### Key Figures

| Player | Performance |
|---|---|
| Jacob Bethell (ENG) | 76* off 46 (5×4, 5×6) — Player of the Match |
| Arshdeep Singh (IND) | 3/40 in 4 overs |
| Sam Curran (ENG) | 3/33 in 4 overs |
| Ishan Kishan (IND) | 49 off 40 |
| Ravi Bishnoi (IND) | 0/60 in 4 overs |
| Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (IND) | 14 off 10 (2×6) on debut |

*Sources: Reuters, CricketWorld, ESPN Cricinfo*
